source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Send command: ipmitool sdr elist
Check sensor reading change when temperature increase or decrease.
2. Send command: ipmitool sensor list
Check sensor threshold(upper/lower warning/critical) match with the spec
3. Heat up the sensor until higher than the warning and critical threshold
Check SEL when sensor reach to threshold

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Temperature should have a normal change behavior.
2. All setting should be correct and match with spec.(including sdr type)
3. SEL should have a correct log when sensor reach to each threshold.
4. System should have correct behavior, like shutdown or change fan speed, when reach to threshold.

original_test_intent: Apply a controlled localized temperature change at the DCSCM, cross its specified warning and critical thresholds, verify correct SDR and SEL transitions plus DCSCM-related fan/power/host protection, and prove cooldown, hysteresis and recovery.
original_method: An attended operator heats and cools the DCSCM area while ipmitool reads sensor configuration and behavior; the source does not define the physical sensor location or platform envelope.
manual_activity: An engineer identifies the exact DCSCM component and sensor location, approves and applies localized heat/cooling, and owns abort/recovery. Automation can then time-correlate BMC telemetry, SEL, fan, power, module and host state.
required_inputs: DCSCM assembly/revision and stable sensor/SDR identity with physical location
units, scaling, accuracy, normal range, warning/critical thresholds, tolerance and hysteresis
vendor-approved heat-source placement that avoids adjacent components plus ramp, dwell, maximum exposure and cooldown
independent calibrated probe location and emergency abort controls
expected SEL event IDs/severity/assert/deassert and DCSCM-specific fan/power/host protection behavior
module, BMC and host recovery checks plus maintenance/recovery owner
pre-existing SEL export/retention and clear policy
safety_requirements: Do not heat an unidentified DCSCM location, change thresholds or force a sensor; nearby CPLD, connectors, regulators and board sensors may respond differently from the intended channel.
Use a localized calibrated independent probe and continuously monitor DCSCM, adjacent-board, fan, power, BMC and host health; abort on overshoot, unexpected event, instability or telemetry loss.
Preserve and hash existing SEL/logs rather than automatically performing the generic source clear instruction; keep the first failure and do not auto-retry.
Do not use command-line passwords or disable host verification as in DeepSeek; use approved authenticated management access.
Cool the module to the approved baseline, verify hysteresis/deassertion and inspect the DCSCM and host before any continuation.
A static SDR/sensor snapshot is partial evidence only and cannot be reported as dynamic DCSCM protection coverage.
agent_execution_scope: After engineer confirmation, poll the exact DCSCM sensor, adjacent thermal channels, SEL, fans, power, BMC and console state on a synchronized timeline.
Compare the local probe and BMC channel using the approved lag/tolerance model and correlate every warning/critical transition with the expected event/protection action.
Verify cooldown, deassertion, fan/power normalization and module/host/BMC health, retaining complete raw evidence.
Do not apply heat, select probe placement, alter thresholds, clear logs, power-cycle autonomously or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the DCSCM physical map, sensor/event specification, heat placement and complete safety/recovery envelope.
Operate the localized fixture and exercise emergency stop authority.
Resolve sensor lag, adjacent-channel behavior and protection outcomes, then issue the final verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The two ipmitool reads are useful baseline/polling inputs but do not identify heat placement, create a transition, inspect SEL, observe protection or prove recovery. The SSH secret and trust bypass are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use bounded trusted read-only collection of the selected DCSCM/adjacent sensors, SEL, fan, power and host state synchronized with the engineer-operated localized fixture and probe.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source commands, requirement to heat past warning/critical, script URL and 5/10-minute values remain; the approved DCSCM thermal plan determines feasible timing.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map the exact DCSCM sensor and adjacent risk area, baseline module health, apply a localized bounded ramp under engineer control, hold at approved transitions, correlate SEL/protection, then cool and verify hysteresis and complete module recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact DCSCM assembly, board placement, thermal coupling and BMC SDR package.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record DCSCM/board revision, BMC/SDR/BIOS, IPMI decoder, heat fixture and probe calibration.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor DCSCM thermal limit/location data, SDR/SEL event map and platform fan/power/recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds component localization, adjacent-device protection, calibrated lag/tolerance and explicit recovery without reducing threshold coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Full coverage still requires attended localized warning and critical transitions; read-only sampling alone is incomplete.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Physical/sensor map, numeric limits, fixture placement/envelope, event/protection matrix and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Localized heating can damage the DCSCM or neighboring components and can produce misleading sensor lag if probe placement is wrong.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may approve a chamber, localized heater or validated simulator appropriate to its DCSCM design, but must record actual placement/method, equivalence limits, covered thresholds and any original physical-path coverage left unverified.
expected_evidence: SUT, DCSCM assembly/revision, physical map, stable sensor/SDR identity and approved threshold matrix
fixture/probe identities, calibration and placement photos or records with ramp/dwell/max/abort/cooldown plan
timestamped local probe, DCSCM and adjacent sensor traces
complete SEL warning/critical assert/deassert entries mapped to expected event data
fan, power, module and host/console protection-state timeline
baseline log export/hash plus no-unapproved-clear record
cooldown/hysteresis/deassert, visual/module health, restored BMC/host state, coverage statement and engineer verdict

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation and target class are identifiable: localized DCSCM heating across Project-defined thresholds followed by recovery. Exact location, limits, fixture and expected responses are normal platform readiness inputs; with engineer-controlled setup, monitoring is automatable, so permanent BLOCKED is not justified.

review_improvement: Makes this specifically a DCSCM-localized thermal validation with sensor-location proof, adjacent-device safeguards and module recovery, rather than a generic temperature template.
independent_technical_reasoning: The DCSCM target materially changes stimulus placement and damage modes, but not the review classification: an engineer can supply the exact assembly map and approved envelope. Once supplied, software can collect deterministic transition evidence. The missing platform values therefore affect readiness, not whether the test can ever be executed.
